result.summary: All 21 fixed nonconstant supports have trivial natural stabilizer, and every nonidentity cyclic action requires more pool deletions than the old pool permits. Weak full-group witness transport succeeds on 133 of147 natural interface orbits, covering246 of283 cases, yielding170 printed representatives with37 fallbacks in both tested pool versions. All313 common protected intersections remain valid.

methods: verify current relevant nonconstant literal cycles/seeds/pools equal frozen originals
enumerate all natural boundary actions and exact cycle/common-seed support stabilizers
compute maximal cyclic-invariant seed-compatible edge cores and forced pool-deletion bounds
identify transported target components by full restored state sets
verify both pool versions retain common K at every original313 interface
explicitly verify every successful family image against actual source and target K
save individual valid witnesses for every fallback
verify four/two pools are subsets of old pools and preserve seed-cut/reserve requirements
limitations: support impossibility applies to fixed cycles/seeds and natural actions, not all possible replacements
170 representatives are a finite print-compression candidate, not a proven simpler analytic method
full-group weak transport failure does not exclude proper-subgroup or favorable-coset compression
no whole source/target K equivariance is inferred from witness transport
pigeonhole counts have no general analytic raw-edge lower bound
manuscript and formal MRS records were not changed
